title: Harcourt Trophies Grade 2 Practice Book — Selected Pages

worksheets.title: A Day at the Zoo — Phonograms: -id, -ide

features.illustration: large B&W line art (chameleon scene, ~40% of page)
features.schoolHomeConnection: Invite your child to draw pictures of animals riding, sliding, and hiding. Help him or her write sentences to go with them.

worksheets.title: Spelling Words Sort — Words with ame / ake

layout.visualHierarchy: balanced — word bank and sort grid equal weight

worksheets.title: Author's Purpose — Read signs and identify purpose

realWorldTextExamples: BE ON TIME FOR SCHOOL! (informational sign)
features.illustration: boy at bus stop, circus clown poster with stars
features.schoolHomeConnection: Look at a few types of writing with your child, such as recipes, invitations, and advertisements. Ask your child why the author wrote each type.

worksheets.title: Picture Labels — Inflections: -ed
worksheets.linkedStory: Henry and Mudge Under the Yellow Moon

features.illustration: 4 distinct scene illustrations (dog barking, mailbox, test-taking, house-painting)
features.schoolHomeConnection: Act out one of the action words. Challenge your child to guess the correct word. Encourage your child to act out an action for you to guess.

worksheets.title: Spelling Words Sort — Words with ed
worksheets.linkedStory: Henry and Mudge Under the Yellow Moon

layout.visualHierarchy: balanced — word bank and sort grid equal weight

features.schoolHomeConnection: Encourage your child to think of a story that uses many of the phonics words. Write down sentences as your child says them. Ask your child to underline the phonics words.

overallLayout.visualHierarchy: balanced — illustration and exercise share space without crowding

characters: story characters from Trophies reading series (chameleon, Henry & Mudge, Wilson)
appealDrivers: story connection gives context to practice

schoolHomeConnection.description: Small boxed section at bottom-left of every worksheet with a house icon. Gives the parent a specific, playful activity to extend the skill at home. Not homework — it's a bonding activity suggestion.
schoolHomeConnection.frequency: every page (at least on the pages shown)
examples: Draw pictures of animals riding, sliding, and hiding
Look at recipes, invitations, and advertisements and discuss author's purpose
Act out action words for each other to guess
Write down sentences using phonics words

tryThis.description: Secondary exercise or extension on some pages (the syllable sort under the word-pattern sort). A bonus challenge that doesn't overwhelm the main task.
tryThis.placement: below the main exercise, visually separated
tryThis.purpose: differentiation — gives faster students something extra without making the main task feel incomplete

storyIntegration.description: Every worksheet is tied to a specific story from the Trophies reading program. The practice reinforces skills encountered during reading, so the child applies phonics/vocab/comprehension in a connected context rather than isolation.
storyIntegration.pattern: header badge shows story title + skill label

wordBox.description: Grey-shaded box containing the word bank at the top of the page. Words are clearly separated, readable, and visually distinct from the exercise area below.
wordBox.placement: top of page, full-width or near-full-width

generousWritingLines.description: Lines for student responses are long and wide-spaced, appropriate for 2nd-grade handwriting. Not cramped.

gaps.name: cloze-story
gaps.description: A fill-in-the-blank narrative where the child selects words from a word box to complete a short story. Combines reading comprehension + vocabulary/phonics application. Different from plain fill-in-the-blank because the blanks are embedded in a flowing story.

gaps.name: picture-label-cloze
gaps.description: Illustrated scenes with sentence frames below. Child reads the picture, selects from a word bank, and completes the sentence describing the scene. Visual literacy + vocabulary.

gaps.name: school-home-connection-block
gaps.description: A reusable component/pattern: small boxed section with a parent-activity suggestion related to the skill. Could be added to any existing worksheet recipe as an optional component.

notes: This is a published practice book selection, not a standalone worksheet. Carolyng specifically called out three design features: (1) the School-Home Connection sections on every page, (2) the 'Try This' extension sections, and (3) the general use of space. The practice book is literature-connected — each worksheet reinforces a skill from a specific reading selection. The airy spacing and generous white space are notable for a publisher workbook. Light ink density makes it very parent-friendly for printing.
